products.title: Hygger Aquarium Water Test Strips
products.body_html:
Check eight essential water parameters at once with Hygger Aquarium Water Test Strips. Designed for quick routine testing, each strip makes it easy to monitor aquarium water without liquid reagents, test tubes, or cleanup.

Regular testing can help you spot changing water conditions before they become larger issues. Simply dip a strip into your aquarium, wait 30 seconds, and compare each test pad against the color chart on the bottle. Suitable for freshwater and saltwater aquariums as well as ponds.

Tests For
- pH
- General Hardness (GH)
- Ammonia Nitrogen
- Nitrate (NO₃)
- Nitrite (NO₂)
- Total Chlorine
- Carbonate Hardness (KH)
- Total Alkalinity

Instructions: Dip one test strip into aquarium water for 2 seconds. Remove the strip and wait 30 seconds. Compare the test pads with the corresponding color chart on the bottle.

Important Notes: Moisture, improper storage, or touching the test pads can affect test results. Keep the bottle tightly sealed when not in use, leave the included moisture-control packet inside the bottle, and avoid touching the test pads with your fingers.

products.body_html:
Create contrast against bright green plants with the deep tones of Bucephalandra Dark Velvet. Its elongated leaves feature rippled edges and dark blue-green coloration with a subtle sheen that gives the foliage an almost velvety appearance under certain aquarium lighting.

Use Dark Velvet throughout the midground, tuck it between stones and driftwood, or mix it with brighter Buce varieties to create variation in color and leaf shape. Its narrow, textured foliage is especially useful for adding detail to hardscape without taking up too much visual space.

products.title: Bucephalandra Pandora Queen
products.body_html:

Tuck it into areas between stones, crevices in driftwood, or group several plants together to fill larger gaps. Its compact growth and chubby leaves work especially in nano aquariums where larger varieties can quickly outgrow the layout or disrupt scale.

products.title: Bucephalandra Hades
products.body_html:
Plant your driftwood-focused aquascape with Bucephalandra Hades. This moody Buce features broad, teardrop-shaped leaves with deep green and blue-green tones that vary as the foliage matures.

We find its darker foliage pairs especially well with knotted wood bases, forest-inspired aquascapes, and dense jungle-style layouts. Tuck Hades into crevices throughout the hardscape or grow several together to create darker pockets that contrast against mosses, ferns, and colorful livestock.

Hades is a slow-growing rhizome plant, making it manageable and well suited for low-tech planted aquariums and beginners as well. If you’re looking for a statement plant with the hardiness and easy care of other popular rhizome plants, this is a great pick.

Plant Care & Information

products.title: Bucephalandra Maestro Blue
products.body_html:
Add soft, jewel-toned colors to your planted aquarium with Bucephalandra Maestro Blue. Its longer leaves help fill gaps in hardscape layouts while wavy edges add extra visual interest.

Grow a colony throughout the midground or mix it with other Buce varieties for a combination of colors, shapes, and textures. Low to moderate light levels along with good flow are sufficient for healthy growth, but regular fertilization and CO2 injection can help improve growth rate and overall health.

Like many Bucephalandra, Maestro Blue can display an iridescent sheen under the right lighting. While intense light isn’t necessary, a quality RGB aquarium light can help emphasize subtle blue, green, and jewel-like tones.

Plant Care & Information

products.title: Bucephalandra Dark Phantom
products.body_html:
Add dark foliage and prominent texture to your planted aquarium with Bucephalandra Dark Phantom. Its deep green leaves feature noticeably rippled edges, creating a bolder shape than smoother-leaved Buce varieties.

Dark Phantom is a great choice for adding contrast throughout driftwood and stone layouts, especially alongside brighter green plants, mosses, or groups of smaller-leaved Buce.

Low to moderate lighting is suitable, while CO2 injection, good circulation, and regular fertilization can support healthy growth and stronger coloration.

products.title: Bucephalandra Red Central
products.body_html:

Use Buce Red Central in the midground area of an aquascape where its darker foliage can break up groups of brighter green plants and add variation throughout the layout. Its dense growth habit also works well for filling in open spaces where its subtle hints of color can be appreciated viewed up close.

Like other Bucephalandra, Red Central grows slowly. This makes it easy to maintain and ideal for low to moderately lit planted aquariums. To boost growth rate and bring out better colors, inject CO2 and use RGB lighting.

Plant Care & Information

products.title: Bucephalandra Alamanda
products.body_html:

Like other Buce, Alamanda works well for filling gaps throughout a hardscape layout and offers an interesting alternative for hobbyists who enjoy the easy care of Anubias but want something different. New growth displays varying tones before maturing, creating subtle color variation within established groups. Bucephalandra can also be grown in humid terrariums and paludariums, making this versatile plant easy to incorporate into a range of planted setups.

products.title: Sand Stone
products.body_html:
Sand Stone features soft, warm beige and cream tones accented by naturally layered textures. Its weathered appearance and horizontal striations create a distinctive look, making it an excellent choice for aquascapes inspired by cliffs, ridges, and gently eroded landscapes.

Its semi-smooth surface and easy-to-stack shapes make it simple to arrange balanced hardscape layouts. Whether used as the foundation for a unique Iwagumi or paired with driftwood to create a beachside clearing, Sand Stone brings warmth and subtle character to layouts without overwhelming the surrounding aquatic plants.

- Warm, natural color palettes
- Freshwater planted aquariums, terrariums, and paludariums

Natural Variation
Sand Stone is a natural material, so every piece will vary in shape, size, color, and layered texture. Some stones might be broad and flat, while others feature taller, more angular profiles! Rinse stones thoroughly in clean water before use. Once submerged, colors may appear more saturated.

products.title: Schismatoglottis Prietoi
products.body_html:
Schismatoglottis prietoi offers the familiar look and hardiness of Anubias with a unique twist. Its soft, almond-shaped leaves feature lightly ruffled edges and form dense, low-growing clumps over time, making it an excellent addition to low-tech planted aquariums.

Unlike Anubias, Schismatoglottis prietoi grows best when planted directly into aquarium substrate, where it develops an extensive root system and spreads naturally by runners. It grows well under low to medium lighting without requiring CO2, making it an approachable choice for hobbyists ready to branch out into rooted aquarium plants.

Plant Care & Information

products.title: Cryptocoryne Spiralis 'Nari'
products.body_html:
Add height and organic movement to your aquascape with Cryptocoryne spiralis 'Nari'. Its long, slender leaves move gently with the current, creating a grass-like appearance that’s ideal for the midground or background of nature-inspired planted aquariums.

'Nari' is resilient once established. It grows well under low to moderate lighting and doesn't require CO2, making it an approachable choice for new hobbyists. After planting, it’s not uncommon for Cryptocoryne to experience “Crypt melt,” but don’t let that deter you. It’s a natural transition process that’s often less pronounced in mature, stable planted aquariums. Depending on the age of your aquarium and the type of substrate you're using, we recommend adding root tabs to support healthy root development and long-term growth.

Plant Care & Information

products.title: Full Red Albino Guppy
products.body_html:
The Full Red Albino Guppy (Poecilia reticulata) is a stunning guppy variety recognized by its luminous red coloration, flowing fins, and red-tinged eyes. This variety is a great choice for hobbyists who want colorful, active fish in a planted aquarium or peaceful community tank.

Traditionally, female guppies are more subtle in color compared to males, but Full Red Albino females often show more noticeable color when compared to other popular guppy varieties. Overall, these active swimmers bring constant movement and color to aquarium setups. They're easy to care for and hard not to love.

Full Red Albino Guppies are sold as pairs (1 male, 1 female)

Guppy Highlights
Vivid Full Red Coloration: Saturated red color spans much of the body, creating beautiful contrast against live aquatic plants and natural hardscape materials.
Excellent for Planted & Community Fish Tanks: Peaceful and active, Full Red Albino Guppies pair well with other non-aggressive fish and are safe for planted aquariums.

Guppies are active swimmers that spend much of their time near the upper levels of an aquarium. They may occasionally explore other areas of the tank, but are generally considered a top-level fish species. They are social fish and are best kept in groups whenever possible.

They are also capable jumpers, so we recommend a lid or adequate plant coverage such as floating aquatic plants. Guppies coexist well with other peaceful tank mates. Mature shrimp are generally safe, but they may consume shrimp fry if the aquarium lacks coverage.

Stocking Recommendations
As a practical guideline, we recommend a minimum group size of 4–6 guppies per 10 gallons of water. Avoid overcrowding, as this can increase stress and make maintaining water quality more difficult.

Feeding
Guppies are omnivores and readily accept quality pellets, flakes, frozen and live foods. Feed only what they can consume in a few minutes and remove excess. Avoid overfeeding to help maintain water quality.

Arrival & Acclimation
For best results, introduce new fish into a mature, cycled aquarium. Take extra time to float bags and match temperature before release. Once they are in the aquarium or quarantine tank, give them time to settle in and avoid making significant changes or moving them during this period.

Care & Compatibility
Temperament: Peaceful
Diet: Omnivore
Group Size: 4 or more

Important Information: If using tap water, always treat with a quality dechlorinator. Stable water conditions, regular maintenance, and appropriate stocking levels will help support long-term health and success. As with all live animals, natural variation in color, pattern, and size should be expected.

Echinodorus cordifolius ‘Marble Queen’, AKA Marble Queen Sword, is a large aquatic plant known for its marbled leaves. Its primary light-green color displays a mix of green and cream tones to add pops of contrast and texture to planted aquariums.

Like other Echinodorus, this plant will grow large over time, making it best for larger aquariums, ponds, or open-top setups where it has room to spread out and fully develop. As it matures, it can easily become a focal species or centerpiece plant.

Marble Queen is relatively easy to care for and adapts well to a range of aquarium conditions, making it an ideal introductory aquatic plant. It prefers nutritious substrate and benefits from regular root feeding due to its extensive root system.

It's worth it to note that Sword plants produce large leaves and can shade surrounding plants if left untrimmed. Overall, Echinodorus cordifolius ‘Marble Queen’ is a hardy, statement aquarium plant that adds vibrant foliage and natural coverage to larger planted aquariums.

products.body_html:
Mopani Wood is a dense African hardwood commonly used in aquariums, paludariums, and terrariums. Its substantial weight and dense composition allow it to sink much more quickly than many traditional driftwoods, making it a popular choice for hobbyists who want less downtime spent waterlogging and more time building their layout.

Known for its distinctive two-tone coloration, Mopani Wood features bold brown hues, natural knots, and gnarled texture that double as rich character and prime planting points. It’s super durable and resistant to decomposition, making it one of the longest-lasting natural woods available. It is a heavy tannin-releasing wood, so if tea-colored aquarium water isn’t up your alley, consider pre-soaking in advance.

products.title: Echinodorus Grandiflorus
products.body_html:
Echinodorus grandiflorus, also known as Giant Sword Plant or Burhead, is one of the largest Amazon Sword plants known for its broad green leaves and impressive size. Given the right conditions, it can grow exceptionally tall, making it best for large planted aquariums, ponds, or similar setups where its leaves can naturally extend above the waterline.

This plant is very hardy and adaptable, making it suitable for aquarists of all experience and skill levels. Like other Echinodorus species, it is a heavy root feeder and benefits from a nutrient-rich substrate or regular root tab supplementation. Bright lighting and warmer temperatures will encourage faster growth and fuller development.

Due to its eventual size, Echinodorus grandiflorus works best as a background or centerpiece plant in larger planted aquariums. Its large leaves help create a lush, natural look while also providing cover and shade for fish and shrimp. Once established, this Sword plant grows steadily and may require occasional trimming to help manage its size.

products.title: Nymphoides Hydrophylla Taiwan
products.body_html:
Nymphoides hydrophylla ‘Taiwan’ is a fast-growing aquatic plant known for its bright, translucent green leaves and distinct lily-like appearance. Originating from regions in Asia and Africa, this species develops a dense rosette with stems and leaves sprouting upward, creating fullness and gentle, flowing motion in planted aquariums.

As it matures, it can quickly fill out space with its wide, rounded leaves, producing a lush, layered appearance. It easily becomes a focal point in an aquascape, contrasting well against fine-textured plants while adding movement and some natural enrichment for aquatic life.

Once established, regular maintenance is recommended. Thinning older and surface leaves will help prevent excessive shading and encourage healthy development below. Propagation is simple, as new plantlets naturally form from mature leaves—gently separate and replant or share with fellow aquascapers.

Pairs Well With
- Fine-leaf stem plants to create varying textures and contrast
- Aquatic mosses and epiphytes to soften surrounding areas
- Branching driftwood to support natural, flowing appearance
- Wabi Kusa inspired aquascapes with a large, single focal specimen

products.title: Star Wood
products.body_html:
Star Wood Driftwood is a natural hardscape option for planted aquariums. Its long, straight branches with pointed tips create a more structured, minimalist look. With similarities to Manzanita and Spider Wood, it offers a nice balance of texture and neutral color, making it a great choice for wood-focused layouts while still being easy to work with.

Its more predictable shape makes it ideal for center or triangular layouts with sloped substrate. Whether used on its own or combined with stone, Star Wood gives you a clean, organic look that works well for nature-style aquascaping. Pair it with a lush foreground or your own mix of aquarium sand and gravel, then finish it off with your favorite rhizome plants!

Best For
- Aquascapes that need structured flow or straighter branching
- Attaching rhizome plants like Anubias, Bucephalandra, and moss

Star Wood Highlights
- Similarities to Manzanita and Spider Wood in texture, color and shape with straighter branches, making it easier to work with when creating a driftwood focused aquascape layout
- Available in three sizes, making it ideal for standard aquarium sizes and larger

What to Expect
Each piece of Star Wood is unique in shape, branching, and orientation. Natural variations in size, structure and color should be expected. Pieces are selected by size category, but no two will be identical.

This wood is naturally buoyant and will float when first introduced. Allow time for it to become fully waterlogged, or use hardscape, stones, or weights to hold it in place during the initial fill.

Driftwood will also release tannins that tint the water, and a harmless white biofilm may develop during the first few weeks. Both are natural and temporary, and some fish and shrimp will happily graze! Alternatively, it can be removed with a soft-bristle brush and removed during routine maintenance.

For a complete guide on preparing and managing driftwood, please refer to the section below.

products.title: Black Forest Spider Wood
products.body_html:
Black Forest Spider Wood is characterized by its signature dark, charcoal brown hue. This unique feature sets it apart from other aquascaping driftwoods such as normal Spider Wood which is lighter in color and only becomes brown in color once waterlogged. Black Forest Spider Wood, however, will become darker and darker as time passes. As a result, this bold aquarium wood provides a much darker-toned and mysterious planted aquarium atmosphere along with beautiful contrast against boldly colored aquatic plants. In addition, this Spider Wood releases a minimal amount of tannins that would otherwise tint aquarium water for a longer period of time.

Wild twists and turns along with knots define this aquarium wood. Its natural root-like look is commonly sought after by enthusiasts. Black Forest Spider Wood works well on its own as a centerpiece or when complemented with smaller stones at the base of any scape.

products.title: Centrolepis Drummondiana (Blood Vomit)
products.body_html:
Centrolepis drummondiana, commonly known as Blood Vomit, is a rare aquarium plant that is easy to recognize thanks to its subtle two-tone coloration. Native to Australia, this species has earned many names in the hobby, including Eriocaulon blood vomit and Trithuria species. Its unusual common name is certainly unique, but remains the most widely recognized trade name within the aquarium hobby.

It is a true foreground plant that grows in tight rosettes. When fully submerged, it produces short, vibrant green leaves with a signature deep red base. Unlike many carpeting plants, it does not spread via runners. This quality allows for very controlled, intentional placement in aquascapes. Its root system can become extensive, often growing longer than the leaves themselves, making substrate choice especially important for long-term health. Blood Vomit is considered an advanced aquatic plant. Successful growth requires a quality aquasoil, high lighting, consistent CO2 injection, and soft water conditions. Pigmentation can be improved with a complete liquid plant fertilizer.

Because of its slow growth, maintaining water quality is important to prevent algae from growing on its leaves. It won’t propagate on its own, but mature rosettes can be gently split into smaller sections and replanted. When grown successfully, Blood Vomit is a highly rewarding aquatic plant that adds beautiful detail and unique character to a planted aquarium.

Common Name Blood Vomit
Care Advanced
Lighting High
CO2 Required
Aquascape Placement Foreground
Propagation Separate and replant
Growth Rate Slow
Size <2”

Native to wetlands of North America, this aquatic stem plant is perfect for high tech planted aquariums and aquascapers who enjoy growing challenging aquatic plants. It features a unique growth pattern that is compact and almost rosette-like, and spreads horizontally before growing upwards.

When grown in a planted tank with strong lighting, CO2 and a regular dosing routine, Sphaerocarpa develops a vivid color palette that includes orange, brown and rich red tones. Its intense color will surely stand out in any aquascape. It is on the slower side of growth, but patience will be generously rewarded! Provide it with nutrient-rich aquarium substrate and make sure to trim it regularly to encourage new growth and branching behavior. If you're looking for a unique aquarium plant that isn't commonly seen, try this one out.

products.title: Eriocaulon Feather Duster
products.body_html:
Eriocaulon sp. “Feather Duster” is a rare, easy-to-grow Eriocaulon species with fine, grass-like leaves that are perfect for the background of a planted aquarium. Similar to popular choices like Vallisneria nana, Eleocharis vivipara, and Cyperus helferi, Feather Duster provides flowing texture with clean, controlled growth that’s easier to maintain.

Despite the picky reputation of the genus, Feather Duster is surprisingly undemanding. Its clumping growth makes it easy to divide and propagate, and moderate lighting is usually sufficient. Stable water quality is key—Feather Duster prefers softer waters, and nutrients can be supplied either through the substrate or with a quality aquatic plant fertilizer.

For stronger, faster growth, increase light levels and plant it in a tank with CO2 injection. It can easily reach the water’s surface, where you can let it swoop naturally or trim as needed, since it responds well to cutting. Overall, its form, soft movement, and lower-maintenance requirements make Eriocaulon Feather Duster one of our top recommendations for aquascapers who want a grass-like background plant.

products.body_html:
Rhodobryum giganteum, commonly known as Umbrella Moss or Giant Rose Moss, is a unique moss species that produces flower-like growth. When happy and healthy, it forms dense clusters of tight rosettes that resemble tiny blooming umbrellas, adding sculptural texture and visual interest to terrariums and planted displays.

In the wild, Umbrella Moss is typically found growing along the base of trees or on shaded rocks where airflow and stable moisture levels are present. Its growth spreads beneath the surface, with new rosettes emerging above the substrate over time. This live moss performs best in well-ventilated terrariums and similar setups. Plant it in sphagnum or a moisture-retentive substrate without waterlogging and place it in an area that receives filtered light.

If you’re looking for a unique moss for a terrarium, vivarium, or paludarium, Rhodobryum giganteum offers an ideal balance of easy care and uncommon aesthetic.

products.title: Bucephalandra Brownie Jade
products.body_html:
Bucephalandra Brownie Jade is one of many buce varieties. Like others, it is a resilient, slow-growing plant that is often dubbed a great beginner plant for its hardiness. While this is true, Bucephalandra have so much potential when provided with consistent care and stability in planted aquariums.

To grow happy and healthy buce, go back to the basics. Tanks should be mature with fully established cycles to prevent melt and alleviate stress on the plant during transition periods. Plant your Buce in a spot that receives low to moderate lighting and good, indirect flow. CO2 injection and light fertilization can help improve form and color, but tank cleanliness is key! Overall, Bucephalandra is a genus loved by most. These aquatic rhizomes can grow in a variety of settings and observing the transition from emersed foliage to fully submerged growth is rewarding. Colors morph and many species (not all) feature the signature iridescent shimmer when placed under specific aquarium lights. Make sure to trim away old or dead leaves and keep up on tank maintenance!

Plant Care & Information

With nicknames like Red Phoenix Sword, it is a popular sword plant thanks to its rich color palette, consisting of deep green to reddish tones. Like other Echinodorus species, this aquarium plant is extremely resilient, making it a solid pick for novice aquascapers or aquarium hobbyists just getting into planted tanks.

To bring out more ruby tones, inject CO2, intensify lighting and supplement with quality aquatic plant fertilizer. However, this is all optional! Amazon Sword plants are well-loved for their adaptability and are also brilliant in Wabi Kusa style setups and low tech tanks. In these environments, the leaves tend to be firmer with a primarily green color palette. Overall, this is a versatile choice for any aquascape and friendly to all skill levels.

products.title: Giant Duckweed (Spirodela Polyrhiza)
products.body_html:
Spirodela polyrhiza is a larger form of the notorious, fast-growing floating plant, Duckweed. Giant Duckweed features bright green, rounded leaves that float freely on the surface of planted aquariums or ponds, producing a serene, lily-like look.

It is on equal footing with classic Duckweed and provides the same water-purifying power, but is a little easier to manage and thin out as needed. Alongside natural water filtration, floating plants are great for providing shade and shelter to aquarium fish or shrimp and indirectly help with algae control. It is relatively hardy, making it a favorite aquatic plant for beginner aquarium hobbyists. Overall, adding Giant Duckweed to your aquarium or pond is a great, low-maintenance way to grow beautiful and functional floating plants!

Important Note! Giant Duckweed is naturally accompanied by regular duckweed, and the two become intermixed over time. Because of this, each order will include regular duckweed. Separating the two is not feasible and would result in unnecessary plant waste.

What to do with excess Giant Duckweed

This pond and aquarium floater grows quickly, so it’s important to monitor its growth and remove excess as needed to prevent shading of other aquatic plants that need light to grow. When disposing, please do not release it into local waterways, ponds, or down your plumbing. Try composting it or allowing it to dry out completely before discarding in the bin. It can also be incorporated into soil mixtures for house plants or gardens! Thank you for being a responsible aquarium hobbyist and helping protect native ecosystems!

Plant Care & Information

products.title: Selaginella Kraussiana Aurea
products.body_html:
Selaginella Kraussiana 'Aurea' is a variety of club moss well-known for its delicate, lacy foliage. Although these plants resemble ferns, they are not true ferns or mosses! They fall somewhere in between and have several nicknames like peacock fern, spike moss and more. Selaginella species make wonderful terrarium plants and are commonly used for ground coverage or as trailing vines in planted setups.

Like other Selaginella species, this cultivar appreciates elevated humidity and well-draining substrate. It is also suitable for attaching to natural driftwood or porous structures, where it will slowly attach and spread. Avoid placing it too close to or exposed under direct, high light, as this can burn the plant. If you're looking for a low-maintenance terrarium plant that provides good coverage with beautiful texture, this is a great choice! Its growth can be random, so occasional pruning is recommended to maintain a neat appearance. Trimmings can be easily relocated or attached elsewhere to propagate the plant.

Drosera spatulata, commonly known as a the Spoon-Leaved Sundew, is one of the largest groups of sundews found in nature. It’s often recognized for its self-seeding behavior, sometimes becoming a “weed” in Drosera collections, but this trait also makes it easy to grow and share with friends or family.

This sundew forms cute clusters of rounded leaves covered in glimmering, sticky tentacles that attract and trap tiny insects. Like other carnivorous plants, it grows best in nutrient-poor soils and obtains nutrition primarily from prey. A balanced mix of sphagnum moss with perlite or sand provides the ideal blend of aeration and moisture retention. Along with mostly moist conditions, Drosera prefer water that is low in minerals and salts like rain or RO water. These plants add beautiful color and texture to terrariums and appreciate bright light that isn’t too direct. products.title: Selaginella Pulvinata
products.body_html:
Selaginella pulvinata is a lovely evergreen perennial, commonly treated like terrarium mosses. This variety of club moss or spike moss forms dense, vibrant green tufts that grow in a rosette-like pattern. Depending on the age of the plant, it may also develop a "trunk", giving it a miniature tree appearance. In natural settings, S. pulvinata can be found growing on limestone rocks at high elevations, making it relatively hardy and resistant to drier conditions once mature.

One of its unique traits is its response to changing environments. When dry, its fronds curl inwards, almost as if to preserve energy, and once moistened, they fan out and redevelop a rich green hue. Keep it in a growing medium like sphagnum moss or peat moss, and avoid waterlogging. Mist it daily and allow excess water to run off its leaves and into the medium. While it grows slower than other well-known Selaginella species, this moss-like plant is great for anyone looking to add an uncommong addition to terrariums, vivariums, or planted enclosures.

Like other aquatic mosses, Willow Moss is exceptionally easy to propagate—any small piece that breaks off from the main mass will attach to a new surface and produce new growth. products.body_html:
Crystal Red Shrimp are one of the most popular dwarf shrimp varieties in the aquarium hobby. These freshwater aquarium shrimp are easy to spot thanks to their bold color and unique pattern. In a planted aquarium, they pop beautifully against live aquatic plants and are super fun to observe. They are not recommended for beginners and are considered more challenging to keep. Due to their specific water requirements and natural sensitivity to environmental shifts, crystal reds usually have dedicated setups. When successful, nurturing a colony is a highly rewarding experience!

These shrimp are considered soft water shrimp and need slightly acidic conditions, extremely low TDS levels, and stable temperatures between 68–75°F. Provide gentle flow and ensure regular water changes to keep the tank clean. CRS will happily graze and forage, but also appreciate a varied diet whenever possible.

products.title: Black King Kong Shrimp
products.body_html:
Black King Kong first appeared in the planted aquarium hobby in the early 2000's. These freshwater aquarium shrimp feature black, white, and hints of blue hues, making them a high-contrast and beautiful addition to any planted tank. Their patterns can vary—some fully solid, others color blocked or slightly speckled. One of the classic Taiwan Bees, they're also commonly cross-bred with other popular species to create hybrids and unique color patterns.

BKK shrimp are a little more sensitive, but still considered easy to care for. Basic care includes using remineralized RO water, stable temperatures, and pH levels between 6–6.5, along with quality nutrition. Many shrimp keepers prefer sponge filters for their gentle operation and aeration. Otherwise, these little critters make a great addition to any peaceful freshwater setup. They spend much of their time grazing and eating algae or biofilm from aquarium plants, glass, substrate, and hardscape.

Tank size recommendation: 5-10G

Shrimp are extremely sensitive to copper. If using tap, be sure to use a dechlorinator to ensure safety for your invertebrates.

products.body_html:

products.title: Saxifraga Stolonifera (Strawberry Begonia)
products.body_html:
Saxifraga Stolonifera is an ornamental (and very cute!) plant. Commonly called Strawberry Begonia, it’s not actually a strawberry plant or a begonia, but gets its name from its physical traits and growth habit. Native to Asia, it is sometimes miscategorized as a geranium, though it belongs to the Saxifraga family, which also includes Jade Plants. In the right conditions, Strawberry Begonias will put out trailing stolons and baby plantlets. Its fuzzy leaves display a veined pattern with undersides that range from red to purplish hues.

It's important to highlight that this is not an aquarium plant, but it would work beautifully in an open terrarium-like setup. It tolerates most household humidity levels and appreciates moderate to bright, filtered lighting. Intense direct sunlight or grow lights may scorch the plant and cause more harm than good. If you choose to pot it traditionally, ensure your mix drains well, avoid wetting the leaves, and prevent standing water. Otherwise, fertilize every two weeks or once a month. It is fairly easy going and will reward you with baby plants to propagate or share with friends and family.

products.title: Sagittaria var. Pusilla
products.body_html:
Sagittaria subulata var. pusilla is a versatile aquatic plant known for its narrow, ribbon-like leaves that closely resemble Vallisneria. This dwarf arrowhead species is highly adaptable and can vary significantly in size depending on aquarium conditions, making it a flexible choice for a range of aquascaping styles. Under higher lighting, it tends to stay shorter and more compact, making it suitable for the foreground or as a transitional plant. In low light tanks, it can grow taller, gradually shifting into the midground or background while maintaining its soft, grassy appearance.

As it establishes, it spreads through runners, creating natural horizontal coverage across the substrate. With occasional trims and maintenance, it can be controlled to produce a carpeting effect or allowed to grow more freely for a natural, organic look.

Hardy and easy to care for, this plant adapts well to a wide range of aquarium conditions and is a reliable choice for both beginner and experienced aquascapers looking to add subtle texture and movement to their layouts.

Plant Care & Information

products.title: Anubias Nana Tropica
products.body_html:
Anubias Barteri var. Nana ‘Tropica’ is a hardy aquatic plant. Its moderate size is still suitable for nano aquariums, but can also be a great addition to larger planted tanks. It features more compact growth due to shorter stems, and broad, dark green leaves. Like other Anubias, it is easy to care for, making it a great choice for beginner aquarists. Anubias leaves are also on the thicker side, making them better choices in fish tanks that contain herbivores that may graze or snack on live aquarium plants.

An aquatic rhizome, it can be attached to natural driftwood or stones. Its ability to grow without being planted makes it versatile with placement and an awesome choice for filling in empty spaces throughout an aquascape layout. Support faster growth and form with CO2 injection and a liquid plant fertilizer! Alternatively, if you’re searching for a good terrarium plant, consider giving this one a try. Its broad leaves are a perfect green filler and its hardiness is tough to beat.

products.title: Aponogeton Longiplumulosus
products.body_html:
Aponogeton longiplumulosus is an aquatic bulb plant that originates from Madagascar. It offers a bright olive-green color and large, fluted foliage that adds a delicate look to any planted tank. This aquarium plant grows large and tall, so we recommend it for larger tanks or even as a pond plant! When happy, it grows fast and adds lovely swaying motion and plenty of coverage for tropical fish and shrimp.

This is an easy aquatic plant that adapts well to most water conditions. As a bulb plant, it will appreciate a nutritious aquasoil to support healthy growth. To plant aquarium bulbs, bury them partially into your substrate of choice and make sure the sprout tip remains above the surface. If you’re using sand, please ensure you have nutrient root tabs on hand. Be aware that some Aponogeton species go through dormant periods when new growth may slow or stop completely. This doesn’t mean your plant is dead—give it some time (typically a few weeks), and it should reboot if planted in the right conditions.
